Console windows flash when a codex TUI session starts on Windows

Summary

Starting an interactive codex session on Windows briefly flashes several console windows (each well under one second, all within roughly the same second). The same codex in non-interactive exec mode shows no windows at all.

The cause appears to be that codex starts git.exe with CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE and without SW_HIDE, so each git invocation is given a fresh console whose window is displayed.

  • Reported behavior: many short-lived terminal windows on session start

  • Expected: no additional windows; the session owns exactly one terminal

  • Impact: visual noise, and the flashing windows can steal keyboard focus

  • Environment: Windows 11, codex-cli 0.159.2, git from Git for Windows (C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe), default terminal application = Windows Terminal

Steps to reproduce

  1. Have git on PATH.

  2. Start an interactive codex session inside a pseudo terminal (ConPTY), the way an editor or terminal wrapper starts an agent session:

     const pty = require('node-pty');
 const term = pty.spawn(
   'C:\\...\\codex.exe', [],
   { name: 'xterm-256color', cols: 120, rows: 32, cwd: process.cwd(),
     env: { ...process.env, TERM: 'xterm-256color' }, useConptyDll: true });

  3. Watch top-level windows while the session initializes (poll EnumWindows with IsWindowVisible, filtering for CASCADIA_HOSTING_WINDOW_CLASS, ConsoleWindowClass, and PseudoConsoleWindow).

Observed

Eight visible console windows appear between +3.9s and +4.9s, in four bursts:

+3.9s CASCADIA_HOSTING_WINDOW_CLASS  'Terminal'
+4.0s PseudoConsoleWindow             ''
+4.4s CASCADIA_HOSTING_WINDOW_CLASS  'Terminal'
+4.4s PseudoConsoleWindow             ''
+4.5s CASCADIA_HOSTING_WINDOW_CLASS  'Windows Terminal'
+4.6s CASCADIA_HOSTING_WINDOW_CLASS  'Windows Terminal'
+4.8s PseudoConsoleWindow             ''
+4.9s PseudoConsoleWindow             ''

A process-tree trace over the same window shows each burst is preceded by git.exe whose parent is codex.exe, and each visible window is preceded by OpenConsole.exe whose parent is svchost.exe — the Windows Terminal delegate being launched to host the new console:

+3.41s codex.exe   parent=codex.exe
+3.92s git.exe     parent=codex.exe
+3.95s OpenConsole.exe    parent=svchost.exe
+4.04s CASCADIA_HOSTING_WINDOW_CLASS  'Terminal'   <- popup
+4.12s git.exe     parent=codex.exe
+4.18s git.exe     parent=codex.exe
+4.37s OpenConsole.exe    parent=svchost.exe
+4.37s CASCADIA_HOSTING_WINDOW_CLASS  'Terminal'   <- popup
+4.51s CASCADIA_HOSTING_WINDOW_CLASS  'Windows Terminal'
+4.59s CASCADIA_HOSTING_WINDOW_CLASS  'Windows Terminal'

Control: the same codex in exec mode

codex TUI in a pty (how a session starts) -> popups=8
codex exec, no pty                        -> popups=0

So the behavior is specific to the interactive session, not to codex's binary in general.

Root cause

Isolated with a spawn test over the same three launch styles a parent might use for git. CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE is the only style that produces a window, and SW_HIDE suppresses it. Results are identical whether git is started directly, through cmd.exe /c, or through git-bash:

Launch style | Visible windows -- | -- no flags | 0 CREATE_NO_WINDOW | 0 CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE | 2 CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE + STARTF_USESHOWWINDOW/SW_HIDE | 0

Per Microsoft's documentation, CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE gives the child a new console "instead of inheriting its parent's console", and CREATE_NO_WINDOW means "the console handle for the application is not set". Neither suppresses the console's window on its own; only STARTF_USESHOWWINDOW with SW_HIDE does, and that is the combination the children then inherit.

Note that codex's own Rust standard library does not help here. std::process::Command passes flags = self.flags | CREATE_UNICODE_ENVIRONMENT and adds no hiding flag of its own (library/std/src/sys/process/windows.rs), so a CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE child with no SW_HIDE shows its window.

Suggested fix

When starting a console-subsystem child on Windows, either:

  • do not pass CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE and let the child inherit the session's console, or

  • pass CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE together with a STARTUPINFO that sets STARTF_USESHOWWINDOW and wShowWindow = SW_HIDE.

The second option is preferable for children that spawn their own console children, since descendants inherit the hidden console and stay invisible. This is the approach already used elsewhere: Orca hardcodes windowsHide: true at its single spawn chokepoint (resources/app.asar.unpacked/out/shared/child-process/spawn-resolution.js:28), with a comment describing this exact failure mode.

Applying CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE + SW_HIDE to the git.exe spawns is expected to remove all eight windows without changing behavior, since the session already has a console to inherit and the current extra consoles appear unintended.

Workaround

Until this is fixed in codex, no user-side configuration in ~/.codex/config.toml removes these windows. The notify command and the node_repl MCP server were checked as possible causes and neither produces them:

  • notify runs codex-computer-use.exe (a console app) after every turn; running that chain as configured produced 0 visible windows.

  • [mcp_servers.node_repl] starts node_repl.exe at session start; it inherits the session console.

Changing the system default terminal application away from Windows Terminal would alter how the windows are hosted but not remove them, so it is not a real fix.

Notes for reproduction by maintainers

Window enumeration is the reliable signal. A zero count is only meaningful if the watcher is validated first: spawn a known-visible console (CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE with no SW_HIDE) and confirm the watcher sees it. Key detections on window handle rather than title, because console window titles change and produce false positives.

Title: Desktop sidebar: cannot unpin remote threads while their host is offline

Environment
- Codex desktop app on macOS; remote Windows host currently offline, as reported by the user.
- App version not captured.
- Reproduced on two pinned remote threads using the Codex app tools connector.

Steps to reproduce
1. Pin a chat associated with a remote host.
2. Leave the remote host offline.
3. Call list_threads: the pinned chat remains present, but title, hostId, cwd and other metadata are null.
4. Call move_thread_to_sidebar_section with the listed threadId, hostId="local" (the local sidebar), and sectionId=null to remove it from Pinned.

Actual behavior
Both operations return isError=true with:
"Could not determine whether Codex thread <thread-id> exists. Unavailable or failed hosts: <remote-host-id>"
The two entries remain pinned. No manual UI unpin attempt was made; this reproduction is specifically through the app tools connector.

Expected behavior
Removing a saved sidebar pin should work locally even when the remote host is offline. The local sidebar already retains the thread identity and pin order, and updating this preference should not require fetching the remote transcript or confirming the remote thread still exists.

Impact
Users cannot clean up stale remote pins through the connector unless they reconnect a machine that may rarely or never be powered on. Missing cached titles also makes these entries hard to identify.

Suggested direction (hypothesis, not source-code diagnosis)
Resolve sidebar removal from the locally persisted item identity before attempting remote thread existence lookup. Retain cached display metadata or show a clear offline label.

Privacy
Thread IDs, host IDs, chat contents, credentials and session logs omitted.

Prompt 1

Prompt 2 (stuck in queue)

Prompt 1
Prompt 2
Response 1'
Response 2

`Response 1'` is not an identical duplicate of `Response 1`. It is a newly generated response with different wording but substantially the same meaning, which suggests that Prompt 1 may have been executed again rather than merely duplicated in the UI.

At the same time, Prompt 2 appears to have been accepted and executed even though the UI previously remained stuck in the queue state.

This looks like a queue/transcript state synchronization issue that can result in both hidden successful submissions and possible repeated execution after restart.

1. Restart VS Code.
2. Open a Codex conversation.
3. Send the first prompt — it works normally.
4. Send a second prompt — it remains stuck in “adding to queue”.
5. Restart VS Code.
6. Reopen the conversation.
7. The queued prompt has been executed, and a second, semantically similar response to the first prompt may also appear.

### What is the expected behavior?

_No response_

This looks similar to #31336, but the trigger is much more consistent in my case.

The duplicated/reprocessed prompt is always the previous prompt that completed normally, rather than a random older prompt from the conversation history.

### Component

Codex local app, multi-agent task delegation.

### Reproduction

1. A user asks for a live file transfer and adds: “A luna subagent should be enough right?”
2. Codex spawns a Luna subagent with instructions to do only a read-only preflight and explicitly forbids it from performing the transfer.
3. Codex tells the user that the parent agent will handle the transfer.
4. The user clarifies: “My intent was for a luna subagent to make the transfer.”

### Expected behavior

Codex should assign the requested execution to the named subagent, with the safety checks needed for the operation. If it is genuinely uncertain about who should execute, it should clarify before assigning a different role.

### Actual behavior

Codex changed the requested division of work on its own: Luna was assigned investigation only, while the parent reserved the transfer for itself. The user had to interrupt and restate the delegation. No files had moved at the time of that correction.

### Impact

This made the agent's plan contradict an explicit user preference during a live storage operation. It caused repeated user correction and avoidable interruption. The issue is about honoring the requested actor for a task, not about whether preflight checks are necessary.

### What version of the IDE extension are you using?

26.928.31416 (bundled codex-cli 0.159.2). Regression from 26.917.62051.

### What subscription do you have?

Pro

### Which IDE are you using?

VS Code 1.140.0 (stable), Remote - WSL

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64 WSL2 (extension host): Linux 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x86_64 x86_64, Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS

### What issue are you seeing?

With two VS Code windows open, the Codex panel in the second window answers the first prompt. Every prompt after that is silently queued: it doesn't appear in the panel, no turn starts, and nothing reaches the app-server. The first window keeps working normally. Reload Window and New Chat don't help. Closing and reopening the second window lets one more prompt through, then it stalls again.

The first prompt in the failing window logs a lock-release failure (from exthostN/openai.chatgpt/Codex.log):

```
2026-10-01 14:14:44.800 [warning] [IpcClient] Received broadcast but no handler is configured method=thread-queued-followups-changed
2026-10-01 14:14:44.807 [warning] Failed to release queued message send lock conversationId=01a0f607-742f-7e33-baad-1d1a82a875cf errorMessage="\"undefined\" is not valid JSON" errorName=SyntaxError
    at JSON.parse (<anonymous>)
    at e.onFetchResponse (.../openai.chatgpt-26.928.31416-linux-x64/webview/assets/app-initial-4bd9e54bcd58.js:3:1518)
    at .../app-initial-4bd9e54bcd58.js:3:1232
    at e.deliverMessage (.../app-initial-4bd9e54bcd58.js:2:41074)
    at e.deliverOrBufferMessage (.../app-initial-4bd9e54bcd58.js:2:41583)
    at e.handleMessage (.../app-initial-4bd9e54bcd58.js:2:41652)
    at windowMessageListener (.../app-initial-4bd9e54bcd58.js:2:40734)
```

Each later prompt in that window logs only this, with no turn start, request, or error after it:

```
2026-10-01 14:27:16.343 [warning] [IpcClient] Received broadcast but no handler is configured method=query-cache-invalidate
2026-10-01 14:27:16.343 [warning] [IpcClient] Received broadcast but no handler is configured method=thread-queued-followups-changed
2026-10-01 14:28:50.410 [warning] [IpcClient] Received broadcast but no handler is configured method=query-cache-invalidate
2026-10-01 14:28:50.410 [warning] [IpcClient] Received broadcast but no handler is configured method=thread-queued-followups-changed
```

The same pattern repeats in four separate second-window sessions on the same day.


### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. On Windows, open VS Code connected to WSL and use the Codex panel. This first window works.
2. With the first window still open, open a second VS Code window (also WSL).
3. In the second window, open the Codex panel and send a prompt. You get a response.
4. Send another prompt in the same thread, or after starting a new chat. It never appears and gets no response.

No code snippet is needed. Any prompt reproduces it. Possibly relevant config: `[features] multi_agent = true` in ~/.codex/config.toml.


### What is the expected behavior?

Follow-up prompts in the second window appear in the panel and get a response, the same as in the first window and as in 26.917.62051.


### Additional information

Regression timing: the extension auto-updated 26.917.62051 → 26.928.31416 at 2026-10-01 07:51:35 (remoteagent.log: "Marked extension as removed openai.chatgpt-26.917.62051"). The first "Failed to release queued message send lock" appears at 08:06. None of the logs from 2026-09-24 through the update contain this error or any thread-queued-followups-changed events.

Analysis:
- Follow-ups go into the queued-follow-ups path. The send-lock response comes back with an undefined body, JSON.parse("undefined") throws in onFetchResponse, so the lock is never released and the queue never drains. ~/.codex/queue_1.sqlite has no rows in queued_items, so the stuck queue is held in memory only.
- Likely (not confirmed): the first window creates ~/.codex/ipc/ipc.sock, and later windows connect to it as IPC clients. Those windows log "Received broadcast but no handler is configured" for thread-queued-followups-changed, thread-stream-following-changed and thread-stream-following-status-requested. My guess is that the lock request is routed over IPC to the first window, which has no handler and returns undefined. The first window logged the same lock error twice but kept working, which fits it owning the socket.
- Probably unrelated, because they also appear in the working window: expired OAuth for one MCP server, no Secret Service keyring in WSL, 403s from /subscriptions and /accounts/optimized/check, and 404s from /tbo/primary. The "Received turn/started for unknown conversation" and "Conversation state not found" errors appear only in the working first window.

Possible fix: treat an empty or undefined lock response as a failure (release the lock or send directly) instead of throwing in onFetchResponse, and make sure IPC-client windows handle the queued-follow-up and thread-following messages.

It can either block chatting with: > Couldn't load workspace settings > Retry to continue chatting or remain usable for chat while the user's Dot, the entire Usage entry in Settings, and the usage limit indicator disappear. Restarting or retrying can restore these features. ChatGPT on the web continues to work with the same account. ### Observed request failures (UTC, 2026-10-01) The strongest evidence is that unrelated API requests fail at essentially the same instant with Chromium network errors. **Workspace initialization failure, approximately 13:30:43.8xxZ:** ```text 2026-10-01T13:30:43.860Z warning [electron-message-handler] sa_server_request_failed attachAuth=true errorMessage=net::ERR_CERT_VERIFIER_CHANGED method=get routePattern=/wham/work/settings status=500 url=/wham/work/settings ``` At approximately the same time, the same error affected requests for pages, spaces, models, profiles, account checks, conversations, plugins, connectors, files, pins, messaging and pubsub, as well as Local Work executor startup. Relevant sanitized excerpts: ```text warning [tpp-local-executor] Local Work executor startup failed errorMessage=net::ERR_CERT_VERIFIER_CHANGED warning [WindowContext] Thread catalog sync failed errorMessage=net::ERR_CERT_VERIFIER_CHANGED warning [electron-message-handler] chatgpt_pubsub_connection_failed errorMessage=net::ERR_CERT_VERIFIER_CHANGED ``` **Partial initialization / missing Usage, approximately 14:08:06Z:** ```text 2026-10-01T14:08:06.199Z warning [electron-message-handler] sa_server_request_failed attachAuth=true errorMessage=net::ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED method=get routePattern=/wham/usage status=500 url=/wham/usage ``` Usage was absent from the UI in this occurrence. Requests for voices, automations, account checks and other account/bootstrap data also failed at essentially the same time with ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED. Chat could remain partially usable. The `status=500` values above are fields recorded by the desktop request handler alongside a `net::` failure; they do not establish that the remote API returned an HTTP 500 response. ### Authentication observations At least some affected sessions successfully initialized authentication: ```text [chatgpt-account-lookup] authenticatedAccountPresent=true authMethod=chatgpt failureType=undefined hasEverErrored=false result=succeeded account/read -> success getAuthStatus -> success ``` This makes a simple expired-session explanation less compelling, but does not rule out every authentication or workspace-routing issue. ### What steps can reproduce the bug? **Intermittent; no deterministic trigger or measured failure frequency is known.** These steps describe the observed reproduction pattern, not a guaranteed reproduction. 1. Launch the ChatGPT/Codex Windows desktop app (OpenAI.Codex package). 2. Sign in with a ChatGPT account/workspace that normally exposes Work, Dot and Usage. 3. Use the app normally; periodically reopen/restart it and observe account/workspace initialization. 4. Intermittently observe either the workspace-settings error above, or a usable chat interface with Dot, Settings → Usage, and the usage limit indicator missing. 5. Inspect desktop logs for failed bootstrap requests: /wham/work/settings with net::ERR_CERT_VERIFIER_CHANGED, or /wham/usage with net::ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED, potentially accompanied by unrelated requests failing at the same instant. 6. Compare Windows network/certificate monitoring and the web app: in the investigated occurrences, the web app worked and the monitored Windows state did not change. 7. Retry/restart the desktop app; the missing UI can reappear. ### What is the expected behavior? Account and workspace state should load reliably. A transient network or certificate-verifier refresh should recover without leaving the session partially initialized. Failed bootstrap requests should be retried where appropriate, and account/workspace features should recover automatically. A transient failure should not silently remove Dot, the entire Usage entry in Settings, or the usage limit indicator for the rest of the affected state. If recovery fails, show a clear recoverable error and retry action instead of treating unavailable data as absent functionality. The user should not have to restart or retry the entire app to restore those features. ### Additional information ### Windows investigation: good state versus affected state | Observation | Good state | Affected / partial state | | --- | --- | --- | | Chat | Works | May still work | | Dot | Visible | Missing | | Settings → Usage | Visible | Entry completely missing | | Usage limit indicator | Visible | Missing | | Default route, connected interfaces and metrics | Baseline | Same as baseline | | DNS configuration | Baseline | Same as baseline | The default IPv4 route remained on vEthernet (External Virtual Switch), with route metric 0 and state Alive. The next-hop and DNS addresses are omitted for privacy; their values were identical in the compared snapshots. Representative interface metrics were Tailscale 5, Default Switch 15, External Virtual Switch 25, Loopback 75, and WSL (Hyper-V firewall) 5000. - WinHTTP reported direct access (no proxy). Per-user ProxyEnable was 0; ProxyServer and AutoConfigURL were empty; AutoDetect was not configured. No proxy-related environment variables were present. - GlobalProtect was off with its virtual adapter disconnected, and Tailscale was explicitly down during testing; the issue still occurred. This does not rule out all effects of installed network software. - Windows root certificate stores contained public roots and local development roots, including an expired local development certificate. Personal certificate names are omitted. A monitor of LocalMachine\Root and CurrentUser\Root detected no root-store change when Usage/Dot disappeared. Static certificate presence does not establish a cause for ERR_CERT_VERIFIER_CHANGED. - Monitoring found no relevant interface, adapter or certificate-store event during the affected transition. - Queries of Microsoft-Windows-NetworkProfile/Operational and Microsoft-Windows-WLAN-AutoConfig/Operational for the preceding 10 minutes returned no events. **Scope of these findings:** no direct correlation with a Windows route, DNS, interface, proxy, WLAN/profile or monitored root-store change was found. Snapshot comparison and these monitors cannot exclude every brief transition, lower-level driver event, or change outside the monitored stores. Hyper-V, GlobalProtect, Tailscale and local certificates are not established causes. ### Hypothesis / suggested investigation (not proven) A shared Electron/Chromium network-service or certificate-verifier context refresh/invalidation may abort multiple account/workspace bootstrap requests. Incomplete recovery after those aborts could explain why the whole workspace fails in some sessions and only Usage/Dot disappear in others. Please investigate handling and retries of these transient net:: errors, the consistency of account/workspace initialization, and whether failed capability/usage requests leave the UI in a persistent partial state. The logs demonstrate correlated failures, not the origin of the network notification or verifier change. A later `POST /messaging/rooms//messages` returned an Internal Server Error at 14:09:20.514Z. That later backend error is not evidence of the cause of the earlier bootstrap failures and is not the focus of this report. ### Similar reports checked Open and closed issues were searched for ERR_CERT_VERIFIER_CHANGED, ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED, workspace settings, the exact workspace-settings error, wham/work/settings, wham/usage, usage missing, Dot missing, and Windows/Electron network-change terms. - #47791 mentions ERR_CERT_VERIFIER_CHANGED in comments, but concerns stalled task streams on macOS, not the missing workspace/Usage/Dot state here. - #48851 concerns Windows Usage failing with workspace-routing status 432 and missing Chat mode, rather than these net:: errors and an entirely disappearing Usage entry. - #49469 describes Windows organization-settings/startup failures with local thread-state warnings, but does not establish this simultaneous request-abort / Usage/Dot pattern. - #49452 describes a blank startup spinner and other initialization failures, rather than the observed partial account UI and error pair here. items.body:
## Problem

The desktop app exposes installed skills through the `/` menu, but Codex CLI requires `$skill-name` or `/skills`.

The same installed skill therefore has different invocation syntax across interfaces. For users switching between desktop and CLI, `/skill-name` muscle memory stops working, and the missing autocomplete can make a correctly installed skill appear unavailable.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install a skill, such as `wayfinder`, under `~/.agents/skills/wayfinder/`.
2. In the desktop app, type `/wayfinder` and select the skill.
3. Open Codex CLI with the same installed skill.
4. Type `/wayfinder`.
5. Observe that the CLI does not offer the skill through slash autocomplete; `$wayfinder` or `/skills` is required.

## Expected behavior

Codex CLI should discover and invoke enabled skills through `/skill-name`, matching the desktop app, while preserving `$skill-name` compatibility.

If slash invocation must be opt-in, provide a configuration setting. Define how skill names that collide with built-in commands are handled.

## Impact

This breaks established keyboard habits and creates misleading installation troubleshooting. Skill invocation should be consistent across Codex interfaces.

## Related issue

[Make TUI skill and app mention sigil configurable — #30355](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/30355) requests a configurable mention prefix, but proposes `@` rather than desktop-compatible `/skill-name` invocation.

codex-cli 0.160.0 (npm `@openai/codex`, darwin-arm64 binary); also observed on 0.157.1 and 0.158.0

```

### What issue are you seeing?

`--strict-config` rejects unknown top-level keys and unknown `[features]` keys, but it silently accepts unknown keys under `[tui]`. A misspelled or removed TUI setting (for example `prompt_suggestions`, removed in 0.159.0) loads without error, so strict validation cannot be used to check TUI configuration.

- `[tui] bogus_key_xyz = 1`: config loads and the session starts (`OpenAI Codex v0.160.0`, `workdir: ...`).
- `[features] bogus_key_xyz = true`: `Error loading config.toml: ...config.toml:2:1: unknown configuration field 'features.bogus_key_xyz'`.
- top-level `bogus_key_xyz = 1`: `Error loading config.toml: ...config.toml:1:1: unknown configuration field 'bogus_key_xyz'`.

The same acceptance was observed for `[tui] prompt_suggestions = true` and for `codex archive --strict-config`.

Impact: users and automation that rely on `--strict-config` to catch typos get a false pass for TUI settings, including settings removed in recent releases, and the setting silently has no effect.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Create an empty `CODEX_HOME` and an empty Git repository `p`.
2. Write this `config.toml`:
   ```toml
   [tui]
   bogus_key_xyz = 1
   ```
3. Run `CODEX_HOME=<home> codex exec --strict-config -C p "hi"`.
4. Repeat with `[features]` + `bogus_key_xyz = true`, and with a top-level `bogus_key_xyz = 1`.

### What is the expected behavior?

All three configurations fail to load under `--strict-config` with `unknown configuration field`, naming the key and its line. Concretely, the `[tui] bogus_key_xyz = 1` reproduction fails with `unknown configuration field 'tui.bogus_key_xyz'`, while valid `[tui]` keys, including notification settings, still load.

### Additional information

Affected area: strict config loading for the `[tui]` table (`codex-rs/config/src/types.rs`, `codex-rs/config/src/strict_config.rs`).

In the 0.160.0 source, `Tui` has a `#[serde(default, flatten)] notification_settings` field (`codex-rs/config/src/types.rs`). An inference, not verified by a test: with a struct flatten, serde routes leftover keys through an internal buffer that the ignored-field tracker never sees, so they are dropped without being reported.

2. Update the npm-installed CLI; verify with `codex --version`.
3. Try updating the background server via `/daemon`. It fails with updater/daemon exit code 1.
4. Run `codex app-server daemon update --from-cli --yes` in PowerShell. It fails with `Zugriff verweigert (os error 5)`.

- Managed app-server package selected at 0.160.0

- Several long-running TUI sessions attached (orchestrated workers, 40–90 min turns)

### Observed
The daemon received shutdown/drain signals at 2026-10-01 21:20:27Z, 21:31:52Z, 22:21:39Z and 23:22:50Z. The first one coincided with selection of 0.160.0; the later, roughly hourly drains happened with no new release.
Each replacement daemon came up and accepted `initialize` quickly, but the attached TUIs ended with:

```
Automatic reconnect could not restore this session
app-server session could not be restored
Reconnect failed — check the endpoint, then relaunch
```

The TUI processes stayed alive and their in-progress turns never completed. We lost three multi-hour sessions this way.

### Expected
A scheduled update check that has nothing new to install must not interrupt attached turns. After a daemon replacement, existing TUI sessions should resume their threads.

### Request
- Do not restart the daemon while turns are active, or defer the restart until it is idle.
- Make reconnect restore-aware across daemon replacement.
- Log the updater identity, the selected binary identity and the restart-mode decision, so a repeated hourly `Always` restart (updater/selected-binary digest mismatch that never settles after handoff) can be diagnosed.
- Document the supported opt-out (`updater.autoUpdateEnabled: false` in `settings.json`) and whether `daemon stop` also stops the updater.

Workaround that stopped the failures for us: `settings.json` with `"updater": {"autoUpdateEnabled": false}`, then `codex app-server daemon start` (updater stops, daemon not rotated), and launching worker TUIs with `--no-daemon`.

### What version of Codex CLI is running?

`codex-cli 0.160.0`

### What subscription do you have?

Not needed for this reproduction: the harness uses a deterministic localhost Responses API fixture, without account authentication or a real model request.

### Which model were you using?

The fixture config uses the string `gpt-6.1-sol`, but all responses come from the local deterministic HTTP server.

### What platform is your computer?

`Linux 6.8.0-136-generic x86_64 x86_64` (Ubuntu 24.04)

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

Two independent Python `pty.openpty()` terminals with separate `codex --remote unix://...` processes. No Herdr, tmux, terminal multiplexer, or session restore is involved.

### Codex doctor report

Not attached: the available report describes the user's normal home and contains local paths/configuration unrelated to the isolated fixture. The script uses a fresh temporary `CODEX_HOME` for every run.

### What issue are you seeing?

With two CLI windows connected to one shared app-server, a **full interactive command-approval dialog from a child of root B appears in window A**, whose active root is unrelated. The two root turns' ordinary assistant output remains separate. This run involved no disconnect or reconnect.

One observed screen in window A had its own prompt `Reply WINDOW_A_ONLY` and the foreign modal:

```text
Would you like to run the following command?
Reason: Local no-op fixture approval for CHILD_B_ONE.
$ /usr/bin/printf TEST_APPROVAL_CHILD_B_ONE
1. Yes, proceed (y)
2. Yes, and don't ask again ... (p)
3. No ... (esc)
```

The same `CHILD_B_ONE` request was also visible in window B, where it belongs. Example thread IDs from that run:

```text
root A:        01a0fd76-dc71-7ce1-999d-9437052cf42f
root B:        01a0fd76-dc71-7ce1-999d-944679ea62a0
child B one:   01a0fd76-dd51-7051-9ce2-2172f1735746
```

The fixture does not click or accept the foreign dialog, so this report establishes **wrong-window rendering**, not cross-session execution of an approved command.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

The [public reproduction scripts and README](https://gist.github.com/gucasbrg/bac134ac9435b8c08593cdac83a9a214) contain the full source. They create a disposable temporary app-server and `CODEX_HOME`; no live daemon, project, credential, or real model API is used. On Linux with Codex CLI 0.160.0 and Python 3.12:

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install 'websockets==16.0' 'pyte==0.8.2'
.venv/bin/python tui_isolation_probe.py --approvals
```

The harness starts a single `codex app-server --listen unix://...`, launches two actual CLI TUIs in separate PTYs against it, gives each a distinct root and two subagents, and has the localhost fixture ask a child in each root for approval of `/usr/bin/printf`. It records rendered TUI frames and thread ancestry under the printed `/tmp/codex-isolation-probe-*` directory.

From a clean rerun using the published scripts (arrival order is timing-dependent):

```json
{
  "A": {"own_child_visible": false, "foreign_child_visible": true, "foreign_frames": 3},
  "B": {"own_child_visible": true, "foreign_child_visible": false, "foreign_frames": 0}
}
```

An earlier run had a foreign child approval visible in **both** windows. `own_child_visible` can be false when another request occupies the single currently rendered approval dialog; the failure criterion is any `foreign_child_visible: true`.

### What is the expected behavior?

Each window should render approvals belonging to its active root or descendants only. The same account may share history and one app-server; separate root sessions must not share interactive approval dialogs.

### Additional information

As a diagnostic control, the Gist includes a **test-only** proxy that drops `mcpServer/startupStatus/updated` notifications for threads outside each window's root ancestry. Running `tui_isolation_probe.py --approvals --filter-mcp` on 0.160.0 preserved each window's own child approval and yielded zero foreign approval frames in both. This suggests foreign MCP startup notifications may make the TUI subscribe to unrelated child threads; it is not a proposed production proxy or a complete fix.

Related: #48349 reported wrong-window approval rendering but was closed because Herdr controlled the panes and no independent-terminal reproduction was provided. This harness uses independent PTYs and includes generated thread IDs and captured frames. #50233 involves a reconnect path; this reproduces without reconnect.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

VS Code extension "Codex" (openai.chatgpt) 26.5928.31416 (pre-release, published 2026-10-01). The same queue code ships in the stable 26.928.31416 (same build number). Last version without the problem: 26.917.62051. VS Code 1.140.0, with the extension running on the WSL side (Remote - WSL).

### What subscription do you have?

Plus

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x86_64 unknown (VS Code runs on Windows — Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26300.0 x64 — through Remote - WSL; the extension host runs on Linux)

### What issue are you seeing?

Since the extension auto-updated to 26.5928.31416 on 2026-10-01, sending messages from the composer became unreliable:

- Pressing Enter sometimes makes the text disappear from the composer, but it never gets answered. It only goes through after typing again and clicking the send arrow.
- A follow-up that was already delivered stays in the queue as "processing" indefinitely. "Developer: Reload Webviews" and "Reload Window" do not clear it.
- The same message is delivered to the model several times. In the session rollouts we counted the same user text 7 to 20 times.
- The follow-up queue in globalState (`state.vscdb`, key `openai.chatgpt` → `queued-follow-ups`) grew to 62 entries stuck in `sending`, across several conversations.
- The webview also throws a caught `SyntaxError` from `JSON.parse(undefined)` (details under "Additional information").

Settings at the time:
"chatgpt.composerEnterBehavior": "cmdIfMultiline"
"chatgpt.followUpQueueMode": "steer"


### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. VS Code with Remote - WSL and openai.chatgpt 26.5928.31416 (or 26.928.31416), with the settings above.
2. Open a conversation and send a message.
3. Send follow-ups from the composer, in our case often while the agent was still working, so they went through the follow-up queue.
4. The follow-up is delivered, but it remains in the queue as "processing". Later sends pile up and the stuck item gets re-sent.

The cause can be reproduced in isolation. In 26.928.31416 the queued item is created with keys whose value is `undefined`:

```js
submission: { hostId: this.options.hostId, status: `pending`,
              queueModeOverride: c.queueModeOverride, editPosition: c.editPosition }
```

After the send, the item is removed by deep equality against the list read back from storage:

```js
o && await this.#_(e, e => e.filter(e => !(0, QQ.default)(e, r)), u)   // QQ = lodash isEqual
```

Because globalState is serialized as JSON, the stored copy loses the keys whose value is `undefined`, and lodash `isEqual` treats `{a: undefined}` and `{}` as different:

```js
const isEqual = require('lodash/isEqual');
const inMemory = { id: 'x', submission: { hostId: 'h', status: 'pending',
                   queueModeOverride: undefined, editPosition: undefined } };
const fromStorage = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(inMemory)); // what is persisted
isEqual(inMemory, fromStorage); // false -> filter keeps the item, it stays "sending"
```

Session id: not available. We cleared the local sessions while cleaning up. We can reproduce again if needed.


### What is the expected behavior?

- A follow-up that was delivered is removed from the queue once and shown as sent.
- It is never re-sent automatically.
- Pressing Enter either sends the message or keeps the text in the composer. The text should never disappear without being sent.
- No SyntaxError in the webview.


### Additional information

**Regression window**
- 26.917.62051 (published 2026-09-23) removes the item by id, which is robust:
  `f.status===`sent`&&(o=!0,this.disposed||this.remove(e,r.id))`
- 26.928.31416 / 26.5928.31416 (published 2026-10-01) introduced the deep-equality removal shown above.

String comparison in the shipped bundles:

| Snippet | 26.917.62051 | 26.928.31416 |
|---|---|---|
| `this.remove(e,r.id)` | 1 | 0 |
| `submission-outcome-unknown` | 0 | 1 |
| `wasMessageAccepted` | 0 | 4 |
| `editPosition:c.editPosition` | 0 | 1 |
| `e.filter(e=>!(0,` | 1 | 4 |

Timeline on this machine: auto-update to 26.5928.31416 on 2026-10-01 at 07:44 (UTC-3); first affected conversation at 12:12 the same day.

**Second, smaller issue (also present in 26.917.62051 and 26.930.21537):** the handler `queued-follow-up-send-lock-release` returns `undefined`:

```js
"queued-follow-up-send-lock-release": async ({conversationId:e, messageId:r, lockId:n, sent:o}) => {
  this.queuedFollowUpSendLocks.release({conversationId:e, messageId:r, lockId:n, sent:o})
}

### What variant of Codex are you using?

Codex CLI `0.160.0`, official standalone arm64 macOS build.

### What feature would you like to see?

**Mouse capture must be opt-in. Codex should never enable or enforce fullscreen mouse reporting by default.**

The default TUI must preserve the enclosing terminal's ordinary behavior:

- native scrollback;
- mouse/touchpad text selection;
- normal copy and paste;
- right-click behavior;
- link interaction;
- terminal and multiplexer ownership of pointer gestures.

Entering fullscreen or alternate-screen mode must not silently imply consent for Codex to capture the mouse. Rendering ownership and input ownership are separate decisions. If Codex-specific mouse interactions are desired, users should enable them explicitly.

Suggested configuration contract:

```toml
[tui]
mouse_reporting = "never" # default
```

Possible values may be `never`, `auto`, and `always`, but `never` should remain the default. Upgrades must not silently switch existing users into mouse capture. Overlays and fullscreen transitions must not re-enable it when disabled.

### What happened?

After the fullscreen behavior became active, ordinary terminal interaction regressed: selection and scrollback no longer behaved like the native terminal, and the TUI owned pointer events. This made a previously normal terminal workflow feel broken and required investigation to recover basic terminal behavior.

The verified workaround was:

```toml
[tui]
alternate_screen = "never"
```

That restored native terminal scrollback, selection, copying, right-click, and ordinary mouse behavior. Users should not have to discover and persist this workaround merely to retain standard terminal semantics.

### Expected behavior

1. A fresh Codex installation does not emit mouse-reporting enable sequences unless the user explicitly opts in.
2. Alternate-screen or fullscreen rendering does not automatically claim mouse input.
3. Updating Codex does not change terminal input ownership.
4. `mouse_reporting = "never"` is honored across the main TUI, overlays, resume flows, and mode transitions.
5. Documentation clearly identifies mouse capture as an optional capability with its terminal-side consequences.
6. A regression test verifies that default startup does not enable DEC mouse modes such as `1000`, `1002`, `1003`, or `1006`.

### Why this is distinct from the related issue

Related: #48664 requests an independent switch while retaining fullscreen mode. This issue asks for the stronger product default and compatibility contract: **no implicit or enforced mouse capture, ever; explicit opt-in only.**

Terminal applications should not take ownership of standard mouse behavior merely because they enter a fullscreen rendering mode.

### What issue are you seeing?

In Codex CLI 0.160.0 on Windows, the fullscreen TUI prevents me from reliably selecting and copying the effective execution plan while Codex is waiting for approval to implement it.

This is particularly problematic in Plan Mode. Codex presents a potentially long execution plan and then asks whether it may proceed with implementation. At that point I need to inspect the exact plan carefully and often copy it for external review. With the fullscreen TUI, I cannot reliably select/copy the plan text.

This is not merely a clipboard convenience issue. It interferes with the human approval boundary: I am being asked to approve implementation while the exact proposal is difficult to inspect or copy.

The problem is still present in Codex CLI 0.160.0.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Uploaded thread: 01a0fe1b-8b91-7f61-a1b8-dc900279f2de

1. Run Codex CLI 0.160.0 on Windows in the fullscreen TUI.
2. Enter Plan Mode for a non-trivial implementation task.
3. Let Codex prepare a sufficiently long effective execution plan.
4. Wait until Codex displays the final plan and asks whether it may proceed with implementation.
5. Before approving, try to select and copy substantial parts or all of the displayed execution plan.
6. Observe that normal/reliable terminal text selection and copying is unavailable or blocked by the fullscreen TUI behavior.
7. As a result, the plan cannot conveniently be copied for careful review before giving implementation approval.

The issue occurs before implementation approval, while the execution proposal is being presented for human review.

### What is the expected behavior?

While Codex is waiting for implementation approval, I should be able to reliably inspect, select and copy the complete effective execution plan.

On Windows Terminal, the documented normal copy interaction should work reliably in fullscreen mode. Alternatively, Codex should provide an explicit action to copy/export the complete proposed plan as plain text or Markdown.

The approval UI must not make the proposal being approved practically inaccessible.

### Additional information

The issue was reported through `/feedback` and recorded without logs.

Thread ID:
01a0fe1b-8b91-7f61-a1b8-dc900279f2de

This appears related to the newer fullscreen TUI taking ownership of transcript selection/copy behavior. The problem is especially significant in Plan Mode because Codex explicitly asks the user to review and approve an execution plan before implementation.

I am not requesting that fullscreen mode be removed. Reliable copying within fullscreen mode, or a dedicated "Copy plan" / "Export plan" action, would address the immediate problem.

### What version of the Codex App are you using?

Codex Desktop version: `26.909.12148`

The same version is installed on the Windows controller computer and both independently tested Windows target computers.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 with WSL2.

### What issue are you seeing?

I have existing Codex Desktop projects whose repositories are stored natively inside WSL, for example:

`/home/<linux-user>/<repo>`

The projects are registered in Codex Desktop through their Windows-visible WSL paths.

When I remotely select one of these Windows computers and start a **brand-new task inside its existing saved Codex project**, the task does not inherit the project's native WSL execution environment.

Instead, it initializes as:

`Windows PowerShell`

with a working directory similar to:

`\\wsl.localhost\<DISTRO>\home\<linux-user>\<repo>`

rather than executing natively inside WSL at:

`/home/<linux-user>/<repo>`

This reproduced independently on **two different Windows target computers**, using different WSL distro registrations, while the controlling Windows computer was running the same Codex Desktop version.

The diagnostic deliberately did **not** manually start WSL, change directories, modify Git configuration, or repair anything, so the initial environment selected by Remote could be observed.

### Independent reproduction A

A fresh Remote task reported:

- the intended Windows target computer was reached;
- environment: `Windows PowerShell`;
- working directory: `\\wsl.localhost\<DISTRO_A>\home\<linux-user>\<repo>`;
- Windows user context was used instead of the expected WSL user;
- the repository was visible through the UNC path;
- Git root inspection encountered Windows-side dubious-ownership/safe-directory behavior.

### Independent reproduction B

A fresh Remote task reported:

- environment: `Windows PowerShell`;
- working directory: `\\wsl.localhost\<DISTRO_B>\home\<linux-user>\<repo>`;
- Git repository path was represented through the same UNC path.

In another fresh diagnostic attempt on this target, PowerShell could not launch because of UNC working-directory handling, leaving hostname/user and repository checks unavailable.

Again, the diagnostic intentionally did not manually invoke WSL or change the task environment.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. On Windows 11 with WSL2, keep a Git repository inside the native Linux filesystem, for example:
   `/home/<linux-user>/<repo>`
2. Register that repository as an existing Codex Desktop project.
3. Enable Remote on that Windows computer.
4. From another connected ChatGPT/Codex client, select the Windows computer and that existing saved project.
5. Start a completely **new Remote task** in the selected project.
6. Without manually starting WSL or changing directory, ask the task to report:
   - hostname;
   - current user;
   - current working directory;
   - Git repository root;
   - whether execution is Windows PowerShell or Linux/WSL;
   - whether the repository's instruction file is visible.
7. Observe that the task is initialized as Windows PowerShell with a `\\wsl.localhost\...` working directory instead of entering the native WSL execution environment represented by the saved project.

### What is the expected behavior?

When a saved Codex project represents a repository whose execution environment is WSL and whose native path is:

`/home/<linux-user>/<repo>`

a fresh Remote task created **inside that project** should inherit that project's effective execution context.

It should execute inside WSL using the Linux path rather than treating the project's Windows-visible UNC representation as a PowerShell working directory.

At minimum, Remote should preserve the same execution-environment selection/configuration that a local project task receives.

If this is not currently supported, the product should clearly report that limitation rather than creating a task with a partially translated WSL/Windows environment.

### Actual behavior

The project identity points to the correct WSL-backed repository, but the execution environment becomes Windows PowerShell.

Effectively:

`Saved project = WSL repository`

but

`Fresh Remote task shell = Windows PowerShell`

and

`Fresh Remote cwd = \\wsl.localhost\...\home\...\<repo>`

This can cause:

- incorrect OS/user context;
- UNC launch problems;
- Windows Git ownership/safe-directory behavior;
- inability to reliably execute repository bootstrap commands;
- failure before basic read-only diagnostics can run.

### Reproduction strength

This was reproduced on two independent Windows target computers.

All three involved Windows computers — the controller and both targets — are running:

`Codex Desktop 26.909.12148`

The two targets use different WSL distro registrations, so the symptom does not appear specific to one particular distro name.

Separately, an existing project conversation on another Windows/WSL host has been continued successfully through Remote, which suggests the failure may be specific to **fresh Remote task initialization/project-context inheritance** rather than general Remote connectivity.

### Privacy / security

No private repository name, organization name, hostnames, Windows usernames, Linux usernames, account identifiers, thread IDs, credentials, tokens, IP addresses, private GitHub URLs, proprietary filenames, raw logs, or screenshots containing private identifiers are included.

No configuration or security setting was modified during these diagnostics.

### Related issues checked

I reviewed existing reports concerning Windows/WSL UNC paths, WSL project creation, Remote trust verification, and project/thread association, including #28094 and #41463.

I did not find one covering this exact combination:

**an already saved WSL-backed Codex project + fresh Remote task + successful target selection + task initialized as Windows PowerShell against the WSL UNC project path rather than inheriting the project's native WSL execution context.**

Please consolidate if this is already tracked under another issue.

### Reporter resolution: recovered with `stop working`

**This incident is resolved for the reporter through a normal-message workaround.** Sending `stop working` in the affected chat produced a new completed turn (6,954 ms); a native read confirmed runtime `idle`. Later screenshots show Dot messaging working on iOS and macOS.

For the exact steps, timeline, source findings, related computer-access observations, and verification limits, see the [detailed resolution comment](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/50450#issuecomment-5963478359). This closure records the reporter's recovery; no app code patch or repair of the old orphaned turn has been verified.

---

### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.930.21537 (build 12776), verified from the installed bundle.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro 200.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), arm64.

### What issue are you seeing?

During this incident, a durable chat stayed visibly running even though its runtime reported `idle`. Its latest saved turn was empty and still `inProgress`. Pressing Stop repeatedly returned:

```text
turn 01a0fb06-a461-75d6-92a3-198510b7374e is not active
```

Pausing Dot and clearing the goal did not clear the spinner. The user also reports that disconnecting and restarting did not help.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed incident; fresh reproduction has not been attempted:

1. The chat accumulated usage-limit failures on October 1, 2026.
2. After allowance replenishment on October 2, the saved turn still showed `inProgress` while runtime was `idle`.
3. Press Stop: the inactive-turn error appears and the running indicator persists.

**Observed recovery:** sending a normal “stop working” message around 16:31 PDT completed a new turn. A native read at 16:33:32 PDT confirmed latest turn `completed` and runtime `idle`. This recovered the latest status; repair of the previous orphaned turn and Stop handling is unverified.

### What is the expected behavior?

When the server confirms a turn is inactive, Stop should reconcile the saved turn and running indicator while preserving messages and paused goals.

### What version of Codex CLI is running?

codex-cli 0.160.0 (app-server 0.160.0, daemon package 0.160.0-aarch64-apple-darwin)

### What subscription do you have?

Business

### Which model were you using?

gpt-5.6-sol, reasoning effort medium

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 25.6.0 arm64

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

iTerm2 3.6.6, running codex inside tmux 3.6b

### Codex doctor report

Omitted

Relevant line: `app-server running (ephemeral mode)`, Desktop app installed but `running false`.

### What issue are you seeing?

Hook execution fails with EMFILE in a long-lived shared app-server daemon:

```
• Hook failed
  └ Too many open files (os error 24)
```

Logged at `core/src/hook_runtime.rs:653`.

The daemon saturates its 256 descriptor soft limit and stays saturated. From `~/.codex/logs_2.sqlite`, 827 rows match `Too many open files` over three days. `process_uuid` is `pid:NNNNN`, so attribution is exact:

| pid | process | EMFILE rows |
|---|---|---|
| 85044 | `codex app-server --listen unix:// --managed-daemon` | 502 |
| 36429 | child of the daemon update-loop, now a zombie | 294 |
| 66499 | TUI | 11 |

By emitting module:

```
codex_skills_extension::loader::host        281
codex_skills_extension::loader::metadata    401
codex_core::session::session                 83
codex_mcp::rmcp_client                       15
codex_core::hook_runtime                      1
```

`codex_mcp::rmcp_client` at `codex-mcp/src/rmcp_client.rs:576`:
`failed to initialize MCP client during shutdown: MCP startup failed: Too many open files (os error 24)`

Descriptor census of pid 85044, highest allocated fd 255 of a 256 soft limit:

```
141 PIPE      (stdio to orphaned MCP children)
 83 REG       (~/.codex/*.sqlite)
 19 socket    (11 unix, 8 IPv4)
  9 other
252 total
```

The daemon had 47 direct children in clean groups of four (`lean-ctx`, two `cua_node`, one plugin stdio wrapper). 47 x 3 = 141, matching the pipe count exactly. The Desktop app was not running, so the `cua_node` groups were orphans rather than live app sessions.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Run the shared local app-server daemon (default, not `--no-daemon`).
2. Use subagents over a long-lived daemon with stdio MCP servers configured.
3. Let the daemon run about a day at a normal spawn rate.
4. Hooks begin failing with `os error 24` and do not recover until the daemon restarts.

Thread id where the hook failure was logged: `01a0f03b-6ca6-7360-aef6-b3b898ac126c`

The measurable signal is in `~/.codex/state_5.sqlite`, table `thread_spawn_edges`:

```sql
SELECT status, count(*) FROM thread_spawn_edges GROUP BY status;
-- closed    19
-- open     193
```

Only 9% of spawn edges ever reached `closed`. Staleness of the 193 open edges, joined to `threads.updated_at_ms`:

```
  4  under 1h   (plausibly live)
 10  1-24h      stale
179  over 24h   stale
```

Oldest edge still `open`: child `01a06e6f`, last thread update 2026-09-04 15:01:30, 676 hours stale, `archived = 0`.

Fill rate: the daemon was restarted at 2026-10-01 21:30 and reached 252 of 256 descriptors in 21.7 hours.

I then ran `codex app-server daemon restart` and measured both sides:

```
                        before (pid 85044)   after (pid 87895)
thread_spawn_edges      19 closed/193 open   19 closed/193 open
oldest open edge        2026-09-04 15:01:30  2026-09-04 15:01:30
daemon descriptors      232                  262
daemon children         45                   31
helper procs surviving  n/a                  0
helpers reparented ppid 1                    0
```

So a restart does reap the orphaned process trees, but the `thread_spawn_edges` rows are untouched. The 28-day-old `open` rows survive every restart.

One more finding that may matter more than the rest. The daemon's `RLIMIT_NOFILE` is inherited from whatever starts it. Started under launchd it gets the macOS default soft limit of 256. I restarted it from a shell with `ulimit -n 1048576`, and the new daemon allocated up to fd 331 and settled at 262 descriptors with zero EMFILE rows since.

That is the whole problem in one number. Steady state for this configuration is about 262 descriptors. The launchd default is 256. Being six over the line is why this presents as a slow unexplained burn over roughly a day rather than an immediate failure, and why it returns after every restart.

### What is the expected behavior?

When a subagent finishes, its `thread_spawn_edges` row should transition to `closed`, its `McpConnectionManager` should be drained, and its stdio MCP child process group should be gone. The parent should not retain the child's stdin/stdout/stderr pipe ends.

Concretely:
- `close_agent` should be a bounded teardown barrier that waits for `ShutdownComplete` before releasing the spawn slot, and should report a timeout while keeping the thread reachable if teardown does not finish.
- Core session shutdown should explicitly drain the MCP manager rather than relying on eventual `Session` / RMCP-client drop.
- A `thread_spawn_edges` close rate well below 100% is a cheap health signal worth asserting on in a regression test.

### Additional information

`codex app-server daemon` exposes only `start`, `restart`, `stop`. There is no reap or prune path, so the only recovery is a full daemon restart, which loses nothing persisted but has to be repeated about every 1.5 days.

The 256 soft limit comes from the launchd default inherited by the daemon. A CLI-side `ulimit -n 4096` does not help, because the exhausting process is the daemon rather than the TUI.

Related:
- #17806 (closed, CLI, same error, same descriptor census shape)
- #17832 (open, leak persists after #16895)
- #17574 (open, subagent stdio MCP helper trees)
- #17115 (open, stale local MCP wrapper processes after session shutdown)
- #16660 (open, app-server disconnect leaves MCP-backed threads loaded)
- #12335 (open, request for lifecycle cleanup)
- #17223 / #17805 (fixes that do not appear to cover `close_agent` teardown)

This report adds the `thread_spawn_edges` close-rate metric and the CLI-plus-shared-daemon path. No session transcript or project data included.

## Summary

Reporting with the affected user's authorization. A dot-created local Windows task can complete and push its original research implementation, but cannot incorporate two separately reviewed follow-up fixes after the user explicitly expands the scope in the main dot conversation. A bounded local `git cherry-pick <reviewed-commit>` is rejected before execution because the approval is treated as relayed untrusted evidence. This remains unresolved after user-selected Full Access and a specifically requested retry.

Related to #50119 and #40125. Please consolidate if appropriate. This report adds installed versions, the exact local-action rejection category, and observed approval-menu limitations; it is not a deterministic minimal reproduction or a claim of a shared root cause.

## Environment

- Windows desktop package: OpenAI.Codex 26.930.2377.0, verified from installed manifest.
- Desktop-managed runtime: codex-cli 0.159.0-alpha.12.1, verified with version output.
- User coordinates with dot through web and the desktop app; the delegated task runs commands on the connected Windows computer.
- User config specifies `approval_policy = "never"`, `approvals_reviewer = "user"`, `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"`.

## Observed sequence

1. The initial task was scoped to research implementation and excluded historical unrelated UI tasks.
2. The user subsequently authorized parallel related report/refresh work and explicitly approved combining two reviewed fixes into the same draft PR. This did not authorize a main-branch merge, release, installation, or external data transfer.
3. Dot forwarded the exact approval question and user's answer. The local cherry-pick was rejected before execution. The recorded reason included: "The cherry-pick is a bounded branch mutation, but the purported direct approval appears only inside relayed untrusted evidence; the trusted original task excluded unrelated UI work, so authorization remains insufficient."
4. The user manually selected Full Access for the affected tasks and requested another retry. It was again rejected for the same authorization-provenance/scope reason. The action remained unexecuted.
5. Read-only app metadata inspection found the integration thread saved with `never`, reviewer `user`, and active profile `:danger-full-access`, alongside a legacy-looking `workspaceWrite` field. The snapshot postdated earlier denials, so it does not establish which settings applied at those earlier times.
6. On subsequent turns, both the integration task and a diagnostic task still received runtime context reporting `workspace-write` and `auto_review`. A harmless PowerShell check returned `ConstrainedLanguage`; that alone is not proof of the UI setting or its effective propagation.
7. A user screenshot showed Full access selected in the correct integration chat and "No commands" when `/approve` was typed. The user also reported no Approve entry in the unfiltered slash menu. Static inspection found an installed denial picker titled Approve, conditional on eligible denials, but that does not establish availability for a dot-created task. No action-specific approval request ID was returned by the rejection.

## Scope and evidence limits

The denied commit changes only account-scoped refresh error/pending state and synthetic tests. It does not itself push, deploy, alter security settings, or touch unrelated work. Repository instructions contain no blanket prohibition on these fixes; earlier research changes in the same candidate also included frontend code and were successfully committed/pushed.

The evidence consists of user messages/screenshots, saved rejection results, read-only local configuration/metadata inspection, installed version checks, and task-reported runtime context. We do not have approval-service internals, a live effective-profile getter, or proof of which layer supplied the restricted profile. Permission inheritance, saved-versus-active state, and authorization-context transport may be separate problems.

No permission database or security settings were edited by the agent, no alternative execution route was used to bypass the denial, and the reviewed fixes remain preserved but unintegrated.

## Expected behavior / requested guidance

- Recognize verifiable, narrowly scoped user authorization when a dot updates a delegated task's scope, or provide an actionable trusted confirmation route.
- Show which permission source controls a dot-created task, and reconcile the task's Full Access selection with its effective runtime.
- Make an exact-action approval control available when required, or clearly explain why it is unavailable on that surface.
- Clarify whether the 0.160.0 conversation-history/handoff-context changes apply to this desktop/dot path, and the supported recovery procedure without bypassing review.

Private repository identity/content, local usernames/paths, task IDs, commit identifiers, raw logs and screenshots are intentionally omitted.

We are validating a custom-agent workflow on native Windows.

### Historical failing case

  codex exec
    --ignore-user-config
    --strict-config
    --enable multi_agent
    --json
    --sandbox workspace-write
    -C <owned temporary fixture>

  ```

  The runner also supplied a fixture-specific trust override.
- The captured **parent policy was read-only before the child was spawned**.
- The child’s role configuration requested `workspace-write`, but its captured policy was also `read-only`.
- Task evidence was present; the child’s model and reasoning effort matched its configuration.
- This case remains a sandbox-policy validation failure.

### Current environment after upgrade

- Native standalone CLI is now **0\.160.0**, independently verified.
- The read-only `codex app-server daemon version` diagnostic reported:
  - `status: running`
  - `backend: pid`
  - `cliVersion: 0.160.0`
  - `managedCodexVersion: 0.160.0`
  - `appServerVersion: 0.160.0`

Before the upgrade:

- `config/read` reported `sandbox_mode: workspace-write` from the user configuration layer.
- `configRequirements/read` returned `requirements: null`.
- That config read did **not** reproduce the historical invocation’s CLI flags or session scope, so it does not explain the captured restriction.

The inspected 0.160.0 typed `thread/read` response did not expose a defined field for enforced-policy origin or serving-backend identity. We did not resume a thread or inspect private database files.

## Questions requiring an answer

### 1\. Which backend serves an invocation?

What supported **read-only command or API** identifies the exact backend serving a particular `codex exec` invocation or existing session?

Please identify:

- The command or API method.
- Required parameters.
- The response fields containing backend identity and version.
- How those fields are linked to the invocation or session.

### 2\. Is the current launch path supported?

Is native standalone CLI **0\.160.0** using the managed **0\.160.0** app-server a supported combination?

How can we verify that this is the path a particular invocation actually uses?

Separately, is a **0\.159.3 CLI / 0.160.0 managed backend** pairing supported? We are asking for historical analysis; we have not proven that this pairing served the failing capture.

### 3\. Where did the read-only restriction originate?

How can we inspect the **requested and enforced parent-session policies**, including the restriction’s source and precedence, for an invocation using:

```
--ignore-user-config --strict-config --sandbox workspace-write
```

Specifically:

- Were those CLI options applied?
- Which policy layer supplied the enforced restriction?
- Could parent-session or managed-host policy constrain the invocation?
- How can we distinguish an intended restriction from a configuration or runtime defect?

### 4\. What is the child-policy inheritance rule?

If the parent is effectively `read-only` and a custom-agent TOML requests `workspace-write`, what behavior is expected?

Which supported fields show:

- The child’s requested policy.
- Its effective policy.
- Whether a parent restriction was inherited.
- The source of that restriction.

### 5\. Can this be inspected without changing state?

Can the required information be obtained without:

- Starting a paid model turn.
- Resuming a finished thread.
- Changing configuration or weakening policy.
- Restarting the daemon.

If a diagnostic has unavoidable side effects, please describe them before recommending execution.

If `config/read` or `thread/read` is sufficient, please identify the **specific fields and scope** that establish invocation-level backend identity and effective-policy origin. A generic configuration dump or matching version strings will not resolve this issue.

1. Identify the responding backend and verify compatibility.
2. Explain the effective parent and child sandbox policies.

4. Collect sanitized, session-bound evidence before another paid validation run.

## Summary

A plugin-provided remote MCP server is successfully discovered by Codex, but most of its tools are absent from the model-visible tool catalog.

The app-server's `mcpServerStatus/list` returns **24 tools**, `authStatus: "oAuth"`, and `toolsError: null`. In the affected chat, inspecting the model-visible `ALL_TOOLS` catalog finds only **1 tool** from that server. The missing tools include basic read-only operations and no-argument tools.

This was noticed after updating the plugin. The exact last working version and causal relationship to the update have not been established.

## Environment

- Codex CLI: `0.160.0`
- Platform: macOS
- Observed in Codex CLI sessions and a Codex desktop chat
- Model: `gpt-6.1-sol`
- Integration: installed and enabled plugin providing a remote Streamable HTTP MCP server
- Authentication: OAuth
- Codex desktop version: not recorded

Server names, plugin identifiers, operation names, endpoints, local paths, and personal information are intentionally omitted.

## Observed reproduction steps

These describe the affected setup, rather than a standalone clean-install reproduction.

1. Install and enable a plugin providing a remote MCP server with multiple tools.
2. Authenticate the server through the host's OAuth flow.
3. Start a Codex session and explicitly select the plugin.
4. Ask the assistant to inspect its available tools and perform a basic read-only availability check.
5. Observe that only one tool from the server is available to the assistant; connection-status and other read-only tools are missing, so those calls cannot be attempted.
6. Independently query the Codex app-server with `mcpServerStatus/list`, scoped to the same configured server and with `detail: "toolsAndAuthOnly"`.
7. Observe that the returned catalog contains all 24 tools with no tool-discovery error.
8. Restart Codex and create a new session. The user reports that the same partial-exposure symptom persists.

## Expected behavior

Successfully discovered and enabled MCP tools should be callable by the assistant, or discoverable through the supported deferred tool-loading mechanism.

If Codex intentionally filters or rejects tools, it should expose a diagnostic explaining why those tools are unavailable. Successful MCP initialization and catalog discovery should not leave an unexplained discrepancy between the app-server inventory and the assistant's available capabilities.

## Actual behavior

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Plugin enabled | Yes |
| MCP startup in host logs | Ready |
| App-server authentication status | `oAuth` |
| App-server tool-discovery error | `null` |
| Tools in app-server inventory | 24 |
| Tools from that server in model-visible inventory | 1 |
| Read-only availability test in Codex | Blocked by missing tools |

The missing-tool observation was obtained by inspecting the available tool catalog, not merely by asking the model whether it remembered the tool names.

## Diagnostics and checks already performed

- Source and installed-plugin endpoint configurations match.
- A second plugin registering the same server name was found and uninstalled through the host. Retesting still shows the same symptom, so that conflict is not an established explanation.
- No explicit tool allow-list or deny-list for this server was found in the inspected configuration.
- A fresh app-server inventory query still returns all 24 tool definitions.
- Missing tools include schemas as simple as:

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "properties": {}
}
```

- No schema difference was found that explains the omission of all 23 tools. This is not a claim that every schema is compatible with every Codex tool-processing path.
- A different MCP client successfully discovers the 24 tools and performs actual connection-status and read-only data calls against the service.
- The server does not advertise resource support. Calls to `resources/list` and `resources/templates/list` return `-32601 Method not found`; those errors are separate from tool discovery and do not establish an OAuth or upstream-service failure.

## Investigation request

Please investigate the path between a successfully retrieved plugin MCP catalog and the tool definitions made available to the model, including any filtering, declaration-generation, or deferred-discovery behavior.

The evidence points to a discrepancy at that boundary, but the specific root cause is unconfirmed. No server changes have been made to work around it.

Related report: #49758 describes a remote MCP server reaching READY without its tools being exposed. This report adds an app-server-versus-model inventory comparison and a partial-exposure case (24 tools versus 1).

No screenshots, raw logs, credentials, account data, or identifying server details are attached.
